settings.heading: One morning you looked in the mirror and it had changed
settings.body:
For most women it lands somewhere between 45 and 53, and it does not feel gradual. Almost every night cream is built for skin that still does its own repair work overnight, and yours stopped. Noula was built for the skin that comes after that.

You will still look your age. You will just stop looking like you slept badly when you did not.

settings.heading: You moisturise like crazy and still wake up dry
settings.body:
That is not you doing it wrong. A moisturiser sits on the surface and is gone hours before you wake up, which never mattered while your skin held onto moisture by itself. Now it does not. Noula is made for the hours in between, so there is still something working at six in the morning.

You notice it when your face feels soft instead of tight.

settings.heading: Your neck started looking like tissue paper
settings.body:
It shows up on the neck first, and dryness makes it look worse than it actually is. A thin lotion will not touch it, and a heavy one ends up on your pillowcase. Noula is rich enough for that kind of dryness, with shea butter, and it still absorbs overnight.

It will not tighten anything. But papery skin looks a good deal less papery once it is properly fed.

settings.heading: Nothing works the way it did before
settings.body:
Most creams put their best ingredient in last, below the thickeners, in an amount you would need a lab to find. You have paid for that before without knowing it. On Noula, red rice is one of the first things on the ingredient list, and that list is printed on the jar so you can check instead of taking our word for it.

Korean women have used rice on their skin at every age for generations, not just in their twenties.

settings.heading: Retinol started hurting, so you stopped. Then nothing happened.
settings.body:
At 35 it worked. At 50 it stings, flakes and breaks you out, so you went back to something gentle and gentle did nothing. That is not a willpower problem. Strong creams work by irritating your skin on purpose, and that is a trade your skin can no longer make.

Noula feeds it instead. No sting, no flaking, no three weeks of getting worse first.

settings.heading: Everyone tells you only hormones will help
settings.body:
They are not wrong exactly. HRT and prescription creams do things a jar cannot, and Noula is not competing with any of it. There are no retinoids and no exfoliating acids in it, so nothing clashes with tretinoin, oestrogen cream or HRT.

It covers the part those leave alone, which is how your skin feels when you wake up. One step, at the end of the routine you already have.

settings.heading: You have a drawer of creams that did nothing
settings.body:
Some of them were expensive. That is the real risk here and it was never the money, it is being let down again by something that sounded right.

So Noula is sold on 90 nights. If your mornings are no different, one email gets you a full refund and you keep the jar. You only pay for it if it works.
